To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

resistance exercise at HL and LL elevated the expression of mRNA genes involved in skeletal muscles hypertrophy, although, the greatest response was seen in HL, however, no long-term effect from either LL and HL resistance exercise was found on the basal levels of the targets mRNA genes.

heavy load resistance exercise increased Myf6, MyoG, and p21, whereas light load resistance exercise increased myostatin, and no training effect on mRNA expression was seen after 12‐week resistance exercise training.
resistance exercise at light and heavy loads elevated the expression of mRNA targets involved in muscle hypertrophy, but no long‐term effects were observed on mRNA targets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of skeletal muscle hypertrophy and atrophy.
the role that the environment plays in the expression of the genes that control the growth of skeletal muscle and the development of cancer.
the effects of physical activity and exercise on the regulation of skeletal muscle mass and function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
resistance exercise at LL and at HL increases the expression of genes that are involved in skeletal muscle growth.
resistance exercise at HL and LL increased the expression of genes associated with hypertrophy, but no changes were seen over the 12‐week period of training for any of these genes.
resistance exercise at both light and heavy loads elevates the expression of genes that are associated with skeletal muscle hypertrophy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
resistance exercise at both light and heavy load increased the expression of genes associated with hypertrophy.

the short term effect of resistance exercise on skeletal muscle remodeling is similar for both heavy and light load exercise, but that heavy load exercise is the more efficient stimulus for muscle remodeling.
we did not find any major long‐term effect on the mRNA targets we measured, but short‐term effects were seen for some of the targets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of Myf5 and MyoD is upregulated by resistance exercise at both light (16% 1 repetition maximum [1RM]) and heavy (70% 1 RM) loads.
resistance exercise at low load (LL; ~16% 1‐rep max [1RM]) is as effective as heavy load (HL; 70‐75% 1RM), at least in the short term.
the muscle‐building effects of resistance exercise are dependent on the load of the exercise.
